title: Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines) — Underwriting Schedule of Limits by Tier
content:
**Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** are written in six tiers. This schedule sets, for each tier, the range of excess dwelling limit the tier writes, the increment in which limits are written, the excess personal property that may be added, the lowest dwelling replacement cost value the tier accepts and the ceiling on total insurance against that value. All amounts are in US dollars.

## Tier entry

Every tier writes an owner-occupied or seasonal one-to-four family dwelling whose underlying primary flood policy is in force. The tier's lowest replacement cost value (below) is also its entry threshold.

## Schedule

| Tier | Excess Flood 250K | Excess Flood 500K | Excess Flood 1M | Excess Flood 2M | Excess Flood 3M | Excess Flood 5M |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lowest excess dwelling limit written | 50000 | 300000 | 550000 | 1050000 | 2050000 | 3050000 |
| Highest excess dwelling limit written | 250000 | 500000 | 1000000 | 2000000 | 3000000 | 5000000 |
| Limit increment | 50000 | 50000 | 50000 | 50000 | 50000 | 50000 |
| Excess personal property may be added | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Highest excess personal property limit | 100000 | 250000 | 500000 | 750000 | 1000000 | 1500000 |
| Lowest dwelling replacement cost value accepted | 300000 | 550000 | 800000 | 1300000 | 2300000 | 3300000 |
| Ceiling on attachment point plus excess dwelling limit, percent of replacement cost value | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 |
| Deductible applied by the excess policy itself beyond its attachment point | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The highest excess personal property limit is the cap where excess personal property is available (it would read 0 where unavailable; every tier currently offers it). Excess limits, dwelling and personal property alike, are written in whole multiples of the tier's limit increment.

## Notes on reading the schedule

- The two dwelling-limit rows bound the excess dwelling limit; a limit between them is still written only in whole multiples of 50000.
- The percentage ceiling compares the building attachment point plus the excess dwelling limit with the replacement cost value; at 100 percent the two together may equal the replacement cost value but not exceed it.
- No tier applies a deductible of its own beyond the attachment point.
